**Starts** once #55 and #150 are merged. #150 writes the design for the line in `select_user_place`'s reply.

## Why

Laying out a day means adding its stops: meals, attractions, and quick looks along the way. Often the user names some of the places, and these tools let the coordinator add and select them without a worker. San Francisco Day 1, in domain model section 5.1, has five such places.

## Design

- [Tool design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/tools.md), section 2.1 (`add_stops`, `update_stop`, `move_stop`, `remove_stops`, `select_candidate`, `select_user_place`, `reject_places`).
- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 4.2 (must-sees) and 5.2.

## Open questions

- None.

## Do

- Add these tools.
- Add the coordinator's instructions for must-sees, places the user names, visit times, rejections, and moving stops.
- Add the end of technical spec 5.2's bullet on a stay that moves to a different town, which #55 left out since it needs `reject_places`. #55's "Changes to stays" section in `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` ends at "Remove the stops that no longer fit." Add, word for word: "Reject the hotel if it no longer fits, with a reason such as \"the stay moved to Bakersfield.\" Example: moving from Monterey to Carmel keeps every stop and the hotel. Skipping Monterey to drive I-5 to Bakersfield removes every stop on its days and rejects the hotel."
- Give `select_user_place`'s reply a line for each other stop or stay where the place is a candidate, as tool design 2.1's `select_user_place` row says, such as "Oscar's Cafe is also a candidate for Day 1, Stop 4 (stop_…), meal: \"dinner\"." Name each stop or stay as `find_in_trip` does. #152 builds `find_in_trip`, and may be built at the same time. If it's merged first, use its function that names where a place sits. If not, write that function so #152 can use it. Added on 2026-10-26, from #129.
- Add the rule in technical spec 5.2, "When `select_user_place` says the place is also a candidate elsewhere", to the coordinator's instructions.
- Add the last sentence of technical spec 5.2's bullet "When the user names a place", which #152 left out since it names `select_candidate` and `select_user_place`. #152 adds a "Places the user names" section to `src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts`. Add this as a bullet at its end, word for word: "A place that's already a candidate on the stop or stay the user means is selected with select_candidate, not select_user_place." #152's functions that name a stop or stay are `stopName()` and `stayName()` in `src/tools/spot-names.ts`. Added on 2026-10-26, from #152.
- Name the `after` input in the descriptions of `add_stops` and `move_stop`, and say what "first" does, as `add_stay` does (tool design 2.1, "Where an item goes"). Such as: "Give after the ID of the stop it follows on that day, or \"first\" to put it before every other stop on the day." Added on 2026-10-26, from #156.
- A stop's set time takes "none", for no set time (tool design 2.1, "Times are clock times"). #156 renamed `NO_TIME` in `src/tools/skeleton-input.schema.ts` to `DEFAULT_START_TIME`, which is "default", since a day's start time was its only use. Add a constant for "none" for the stop tools. Don't reuse `DEFAULT_START_TIME`. Added on 2026-10-26, from #156.
- A meal's `tierRule` input gives only its format, as `add_stay`'s does: "In a few words, such as \"the default tier\"." What the rule means is in the coordinator's instructions (tool design, section 4). Added on 2026-10-26, from #156.
- Use the terms in the tool descriptions as the coordinator's instructions define them, in the section "The itinerary", such as stop, set, search area, waypoint, and road time. Don't define them again in a description, and add a line to that section for any new line a read or reply shows (tool design, section 4). Added on 2026-10-26, from #156.
- Change `compute_route`'s reply from "Drive times are Google's averages, without the drive buffer." to "Road times are Google's averages, without the drive buffer.", so it uses the name "The itinerary" section gives this figure. Change tool design 2.4 if it quotes the reply. Added on 2026-10-26, from #160.
- Fix the "Leg" and "Day" terms in the coordinator's "The itinerary" section, so they fit the first and last days. The "Leg" term says a leg runs "from where the party slept to where it sleeps that night", but Day 1's leg starts at the start place, and the last day's leg ends at the end place, where the party doesn't sleep. The "Day" term says a day "either moves to a new stay, or stays put", but the last day does neither. As a starting point, a leg runs "from where the day starts, the start place or a stay, to where it ends, a stay or the end place", and the "Day" term covers the last day too. Change technical spec 5.2 to match. Added on 2026-10-26, from #160.

## Done when

In a chat with the coordinator:

- San Francisco Day 1 is laid out with the five places the user names, all selected, with times close to domain model section 5.1. No worker is needed.
- Making the Boardwalk visit five hours gives a warning that the Whaling Station dinner is late, and the coordinator raises it.
- "No Sardine Factory" rejects it, with the user's reason. The Sardine Factory is a Monterey restaurant. It isn't in the example, so it's only there to be ruled out.

And in the tests:

- `select_user_place` with a place that's a candidate on another stop or stay succeeds, and its reply names each of those stops or stays.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

---

Moved from the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md#phase-23-lay-out-days).
